A volcano plot is the workhorse of differential-expression analysis: log fold change on x,
statistical significance on y, and the interesting genes pushed out to the top corners. In
this post we build one in R with [canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org) — interactive
(zoom, hover, filter), and, importantly, **reproducible**: the whole figure is a single
portable specification you can store, validate and re-render from R, Python or JavaScript.

## Install

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("canvasXpress")
```

## A differential-expression table

For a self-contained example we simulate 1,000 genes. Swap this block for your own results
table (e.g. the output of `limma::topTable()` or `DESeq2::results()`) — you need a log fold
change and a significance value per gene.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(1)
n       <- 1000
genes   <- paste0("Gene", seq_len(n))
logFC   <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.8)
negLogP <- -log10(runif(n)^1.5)   # stand-in for -log10(p-value)

# Classify each gene by effect size + significance
group <- ifelse(logFC >  1 & negLogP > 2, "Increased",
         ifelse(logFC < -1 & negLogP > 2, "Decreased", "NoChange"))
```

canvasXpress expects a numeric matrix/data frame of values (genes in rows) plus an optional
**variable annotation** table carrying per-gene attributes — here the regulation call and the
fold change we'll use for point size.

```{r}
y <- data.frame(
  "logFC"     = logFC,
  "-log-pVal" = negLogP,
  row.names   = genes,
  check.names = FALSE
)

varAnnot <- data.frame(
  Group = group,
  FC    = round(2^abs(logFC), 2),
  row.names   = genes,
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

## The plot

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data     = y,
  varAnnot = varAnnot,
  graphType = "Scatter2D",
  xAxis    = list("logFC"),
  yAxis    = list("-log-pVal"),
  colorBy  = "Group",
  colorKey = list(Group = list(
    Increased = "rgba(197,27,38,0.75)",
    Decreased = "rgba(33,102,172,0.75)",
    NoChange  = "rgba(150,150,150,0.35)"
  )),
  sizeBy   = "FC",
  sizes    = c(3, 6, 9, 12, 15),
  title    = "Publication-ready volcano plot",
  xAxisTitle = "log2 fold change",
  yAxisTitle = "-log10 p-value",
  showDecorations = TRUE,
  decorations = list(line = list(
    list(color = "rgba(120,120,120,0.8)", width = 1, x =  1),
    list(color = "rgba(120,120,120,0.8)", width = 1, x = -1),
    list(color = "rgba(120,120,120,0.8)", width = 1, y = 1.301)
  )),
  width  = 650,
  height = 500
)
```

The chart is interactive: hover a point for its gene and values, drag to zoom, or use the
toolbar to filter by regulation group. The dashed guides mark the ±1 log2FC and the p = 0.05
cutoffs.

## Why "reproducible"

Everything above serializes to one JSON specification — the `data` and the `config`. That
spec is portable: the identical figure renders from the Python (`canvasxpress`) and
JavaScript packages, and it can be validated against a published schema and re-rendered later,
so a figure in a paper can be regenerated and audited rather than just looked at.
